title: Viva Engage: sensitivity labels for communities (Microsoft Purview)
summary: The briefing's rollout facts, licensing statements and governance mechanisms are supported by the roadmap and Microsoft documentation. The two Purview navigation paths reach the correct pages but should continue to the controls inside the label and publishing wizards.

claims.claim: Viva Engage communities support Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: After you configure sensitivity labels with their associated policies in the Microsoft Purview portal, these labels can be applied to communities in your organization.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes manual application of Information Protection sensitivity labels in Engage.
claims.quote: Your organization can now manually apply Information Protection sensitivity labels in Engage.

claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators can create labels.
claims.quote: Sensitivity label support in this new application will allow admins to create labels

claims.claim: The roadmap says publishing policies determine which users and groups can manually label content in Engage.
claims.quote: configure label publishing policies to determine which users and groups can manually label content in Engage.

claims.claim: The roadmap says end users can apply labels to Engage communities.
claims.quote: End users will be able to manually apply labels to Engage communities

claims.claim: The roadmap describes classification and protection through privacy and external user access controls.
claims.quote: classify and protect their sensitive data via privacy and external user access controls.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2025.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2025"

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is September CY2025.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2025"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Sensitivity label privacy settings govern Engage communities.
claims.quote: Community admins can change the sensitivity label (and hence its privacy setting) of a community.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[1].governs
claims.claim: Sensitivity labels control guest access to Engage communities.
claims.quote: Use sensitivity labels to control guest access to your communities.

claims.claim: Labels and their associated policies are configured in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: After you configure sensitivity labels with their associated policies in the Microsoft Purview portal, these labels can be applied to communities in your organization.

claims.claim: An administrator can choose an Engage community default label in label policy settings.
claims.quote: select a preferred default label for Engage communities in Microsoft Purview as part of label policy settings.

claims.claim: The Engage default takes precedence over the default label for sites.
claims.quote: This new default takes precedence over the default label for sites.

claims.claim: Engage can use a more permissive default than SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Create a more permissive default for Engage communities, while maintaining a more restrictive default for sites.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy; rationale: risk, impact
claims.claim: A configured default label automatically applies during community creation.
claims.quote: Admins can set up sensitivity labels to automatically apply during community creation. When a user creates a new community, the default sensitivity label automatically applies to the community.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The person creating a community can select a different available label.
claims.quote: The user can select a different label from the list of available labels

claims.claim: Community creators cannot create new labels through label selection.
claims.quote: The user can select a different label from the list of available labels, but they can't create new labels.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Community administrators can change a community's sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Community admins can change the sensitivity label (and hence its privacy setting) of a community.

claims.claim: Users see the sensitivity label in the community banner.
claims.quote: After the community is live, the sensitivity label appears to users in the community banner

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A Public or Private label setting sets and locks container privacy.
claims.quote: The settings of Public or Private set and lock the privacy setting when you apply this label to the container.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The label must first be removed to change the locked privacy setting.
claims.quote: locks the privacy value so it can be changed only by first removing the sensitivity label from the container.

claims.claim: Communities created with a label prohibiting guest access are available only within the organization.
claims.quote: Communities created with a label that doesn’t allow guest access are only available to users in your organization. People outside your organization can’t be added to the community.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Items inside a labeled container do not inherit its label.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A container label does not apply item-level encryption.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels and therefore don't apply any item-level label settings, such as content markings and encryption.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A container label does not apply item-level content markings.
claims.quote: Items in these containers however, do not inherit the labels and therefore don't apply any item-level label settings, such as content markings and encryption.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Engage documentation says PowerShell does not directly specify community sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: PowerShell cmdlets don't directly support sensitivity labels. Users can't directly specify sensitivity labels for Engage communities.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The documented PowerShell workaround labels the connected SharePoint site to update the existing Engage community.
claims.quote: As a workaround, you can use PowerShell to apply labels to a SharePoint site that connects to an existing Engage community. Doing so causes the label on the Engage community to correspondingly update.

claims.claim: The Viva compliance overview also documents Purview sensitivity label support in Engage.
claims.quote: The Viva Engage features eDiscovery, Data Retention, and sensitivity labels are supported by Microsoft Purview; data loss prevention isn't supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Engage as public-first in many organizations.
claims.quote: Engage is a public-first platform in many organizations.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Labels are unavailable for selection until they are published through a label policy.
claims.quote: Until you publish your labels, they won't be available to select in apps or for services. To publish the labels, they must be added to a label policy.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Container label settings are visible but cannot be configured before container labeling is enabled.
claims.quote: Until sensitivity labels are enabled for containers, the settings are visible but you can't configure them.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in, requiring container enablement and label configuration.
claims.quote: After you enable and configure sensitivity labels for containers, users can additionally see and apply sensitivity labels to containers that support them.

claims.claim: Container label enablement is a one-time procedure.
claims.quote: If you haven't yet enabled sensitivity labels for containers, do the following set of steps as a one-time procedure

claims.claim: Supported containers include Teams sites, Microsoft 365 groups, SharePoint sites and Viva Engage communities.
claims.quote: These include Microsoft team sites, Microsoft 365 groups, SharePoint sites, Viva Engage communities, and Loop workspaces.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Public as allowing anyone in the organization access to the container.
claims.quote: Privacy: Keep the default of Public if you want anyone in your organization to access the container where this label is applied.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Engage example uses a Public privacy label as the Engage default.
claims.quote: New Engage communities prepopulate with the General label (privacy setting of Public).

claims.claim: Clearing a label's external user access setting does not revoke existing guests' access.
claims.quote: The new setting applies to new users but not to existing users. For example, if this setting was previously selected and as a result, guest users accessed the site, these guest users can still access the site after this setting is cleared in the label configuration.

claims.claim: Configuring external sharing in a label can delegate otherwise administrator-restricted choices to site owners.
claims.quote: When you configure and publish the label settings for external sharing options and the authentication context, a site owner can now set and change these options for a site by applying or changing the sensitivity label for a team or site.

claims.claim: Configuring authentication context in a label can likewise extend those choices to site owners.
claims.quote: When you configure and publish the label settings for external sharing options and the authentication context, a site owner can now set and change these options for a site by applying or changing the sensitivity label for a team or site.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises allowing 24 hours for label and policy propagation before troubleshooting.
claims.quote: For labels and label policy settings, allow 24 hours for the changes to propagate through the services.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises against changing site and group settings after labels have been applied.
claims.quote: As a best practice, don't change the site and group settings for a sensitivity label after the label has been applied to teams, groups, or sites.

claims.claim: The Entra documentation says published group-setting changes are not automatically applied to labeled groups.
claims.quote: When you make changes to group settings for a published label in the Microsoft Purview portal, those policy changes aren't automatically applied on the labeled groups.

claims.claim: The Entra documentation calls for manually applying necessary updates to affected groups.
claims.quote: If you must make a change, use a PowerShell script to manually apply updates to the affected groups.

claims.claim: Deleting a site-and-group label while it remains in a publishing policy can cause new container creation failures.
claims.quote: If you delete a sensitivity label that has the site and group settings enabled, and that label is included in one or more label policies, this action can result in creation failures for new teams, groups, and sites.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft's safe deletion procedure first removes the label from all label policies.
claims.quote: Remove the sensitivity label from all label policies that include the label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The deletion procedure requires waiting at least one hour after removing the label from policies.
claims.quote: Wait at least one hour.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The deletion procedure then tests creation of a team, group or site and verifies the label is no longer visible.
claims.quote: After this wait period, try creating a team, group, or site and confirm that the label is no longer visible.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The label should be deleted only after that visibility check succeeds.
claims.quote: If the sensitivity label isn't visible, you can now safely delete the label.

claims.claim: Users need subscriptions supporting the sensitivity labeling functionality they use.
claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services, and the licensing requirements for users depend on the features you use.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cited service description marks Manual Sensitivity Labeling Included for the listed Microsoft 365 plans.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3/F1/F3/Business Premium ... | Manual Sensitivity Labeling | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |

claims.claim: Information Protection for Office 365 and AIP require Standard/Plan 1 assignment alongside Premium/Plan 2.
claims.quote: A standard/Plan 1 license must be assigned in addition to the premium/P2 license for users to have access to sensitivity labeling for Information Protection for Office 365 and AIP, even if the premium licenses/Plan 2 are assigned.

claims.claim: An AIP P2 user must also have AIP P1 assigned.
claims.quote: And if AIP P2 is assigned to a user, that user must also have AIP P1 assigned.

claims.claim: The same service description also states an E5 or IPG requirement for sensitivity labeling including automatic or policy-based labeling.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: Administrators also need a license to manage sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Admins also need a license to manage sensitivity labels.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; controls[0].note; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Configuring Microsoft 365 group sensitivity labels requires at least one active Entra ID P1 license in the tenant.
claims.quote: To configure this feature, there must be at least one active Microsoft Entra ID P1 license in your Microsoft Entra organization.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Viva Engage sensitivity labels page itself names no license requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage community sensitivity labels license licensing Microsoft Entra P1; opened the complete community-sensitivity-labeling page, get-started-with-sensitivity-labels, groups-assign-sensitivity-labels and the Purview service description. The Engage feature page names no license.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included in qualifying sensitivity-labeling subscriptions.
claims.quote: | Manual Sensitivity Labeling | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |

claims.claim: Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator and Security Administrator role groups are documented options for creating and configuring labels and policies.
claims.quote: Another option is to add users to the Compliance Data Administrator, Compliance Administrator, or Security Administrator role group.

claims.claim: A custom role group containing Sensitivity Label Administrator is another documented option.
claims.quote: Alternatively to using the default role groups, you can create a new role group and add the Sensitivity Label Administrator role to this group.

claims.claim: These label-management permissions are not required merely to apply labels.
claims.quote: These permissions are required only to create and configure sensitivity labels and their label policies. They are not required to apply the labels in apps or services.

claims.claim: Users assigned a publishing policy containing a label can select that label for sites and groups.
claims.quote: The users who are assigned a sensitivity label policy that includes this label will be able to select it for sites and groups.

claims.where: Scope, final paragraph; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Group and site labeling requires the Groups & sites label scope.
claims.quote: Follow the general instructions to create or edit a sensitivity label and make sure you select Groups & sites for the label's scope

claims.claim: Publication in the tenant's Purview portal is a prerequisite for group label assignment.
claims.quote: The sensitivity labels are published in the Microsoft Purview portal or the Microsoft Purview portal for this Microsoft Entra organization.

claims.where: Scope, final paragraph; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: EnableMIPLabels must be True for group sensitivity labeling.
claims.quote: The feature is enabled and EnableMIPLabels is set to True in the Microsoft Graph PowerShell module.

claims.claim: Execute-AzureAdLabelSync in Security & Compliance PowerShell synchronizes sensitivity labels to Entra ID.
claims.quote: Labels are synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID with the Execute-AzureAdLabelSync cmdlet in the Security & Compliance PowerShell module.

claims.claim: Labels can take up to 24 hours after synchronization to become available in Entra ID.
claims.quote: It can take up to 24 hours after synchronization for the label to be available to Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: Reading EnableMIPLabels identifies whether container labeling was already enabled.
claims.quote: If the sensitivity label was enabled previously, you see EnableMIPLabels = True. In this case, you don't need to do anything.

claims.claim: Microsoft's pilot procedure publishes to a few test users, waits for replication and tests creation of a team, group or SharePoint site.
claims.quote: add this label to a label policy that applies to just a few test users. ... After this wait period, use one of the test user accounts to create a team, Microsoft 365 group, or SharePoint site with the label that you created in step 1.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends targeting groups instead of individual users for lower publishing-policy maintenance.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings. For lower administrative maintenance, groups are recommended rather than individual users.

claims.claim: Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting with DirectorySettingId and BodyParameter can enable tenant group labeling by setting EnableMIPLabels to True.
claims.quote:
Name = "EnableMIPLabels"
Value = "True" ... Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $grpUnifiedSetting.Id -BodyParameter $params

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for setting the tenant EnableMIPLabels prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: EnableMIPLabels enable sensitivity labels containers admin center UI; opened groups-assign-sensitivity-labels and sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites. Both use PowerShell. The Engage disable-labels UI is a different control, not the Entra EnableMIPLabels prerequisite.

claims.claim: Purview Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels reaches the page used to configure label privacy and guest access.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels ... To edit an existing label, select it, and then select the Edit label icon.
claims.fix: For an existing label, extend the path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Groups & sites > Define protection settings for groups and sites > Privacy and external user access settings > Privacy / External user access'. The last wizard steps are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites, already cited by the briefing.

claims.claim: New-Label creates a sensitivity label using the printed Name, ContentType and site-and-group protection parameters.
claims.quote: Use the New-Label cmdlet to create sensitivity labels in your organization. ... [-ContentType <MipLabelContentType>] ... [-SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled <System.Boolean>]

claims.claim: ContentType permits the combined value "Site, UnifiedGroup".
claims.quote: The ContentType parameter specifies where the sensitivity label can be applied. Valid values are: ... Site ... UnifiedGroup ... Values can be combined, for example: "File, Email, PurviewAssets".

claims.claim: SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled $true enables the label's site-and-group protection action.
claims.quote: The SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled parameter enables or disables the Site and Group Protection action for the label. Valid values are: ... $true: The Site and Group Protection action is enabled.

claims.claim: SiteAndGroupProtectionPrivacy accepts Public or Private.
claims.quote: The SiteAndGroupProtectionPrivacy parameter specifies the privacy level for the labe. Valid values are: ... Public ... Private

claims.claim: SiteAndGroupProtectionAllowAccessToGuestUsers takes a Boolean controlling guest access.
claims.quote: The SiteAndGroupProtectionAllowAccessToGuestUsers parameter enables or disables access to guest users. Valid values are: ... $true: Guest access is enabled. ... $false: Guest access is disabled.

claims.claim: New-Label is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Purview Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies reaches the label publishing policy page.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... On the Label policies page, select Publish label to start the Create policy configuration.
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label > Choose sensitivity labels to publish > Choose sensitivity labels to publish', where the labels are selected. Keep recipient and policy-setting choices described in the existing note. See https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels#publish-sensitivity-labels-by-creating-a-label-policy.

claims.claim: New-LabelPolicy -Name <policy name> -Labels <label names> creates a policy containing those labels.
claims.quote: New-LabelPolicy -Name "Research and Development" -Labels "R and D","R and D Management" ... This example creates the sensitivity label policy named Research and Development that contains sensitivity labels named R and D and R and D Management.

claims.claim: The table's New-Label and New-LabelPolicy calls create labels and policies rather than assigning labels to communities.
claims.quote: Use the New-LabelPolicy cmdlet to create sensitivity label policies in your organization.

claims.claim: The Labels parameter accepts sensitivity label names.
claims.quote: The Labels parameter specifies the sensitivity labels that are associated with the policy. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the label. For example: ... Name ... Distinguished name (DN) ... GUID

claims.claim: The printed Name-and-Labels call does not specify recipients or a container default.
claims.quote: New-LabelPolicy -Name "Research and Development" -Labels "R and D","R and D Management" ... This example creates the sensitivity label policy named Research and Development that contains sensitivity labels named R and D and R and D Management.

claims.claim: The publishing policy wizard selects recipient users and groups.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.claim: The publishing policy settings offered match the scopes of the selected labels.
claims.quote: The policy settings that you see match the scope of the labels that you selected.

claims.where: Governance controls, final paragraph; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy; Scope
claims.claim: Community administrators reach label settings by opening the community, selecting More (...) and choosing Settings.
claims.quote: Open the community, select the More menu (...), and choose Settings.

claims.claim: The community Settings instructions present Engage and site default dropdowns whose choices depend on configured policies.
claims.quote: choose the General label as your Engage default label and the Public label as your site default. (Depending on how the policies are configured, other choices might be available for each of the two dropdowns.)

claims.claim: The specific policy setting name for the Engage default and its relation to the groups-and-sites default remain undocumented in the checked material.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage default sensitivity label policy setting existing unlabeled communities default; opened community-sensitivity-labeling and create-sensitivity-labels. They describe the Engage default's precedence and the groups/sites default but do not name an Engage-specific policy setting.

claims.claim: The checked documentation does not resolve what publishing an Engage default does to existing unlabeled communities.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage default sensitivity label policy setting existing unlabeled communities default; opened community-sensitivity-labeling, create-sensitivity-labels and enforce-office-365-identity. The feature page describes new-community defaults, not retroactive labeling of unlabeled communities.

claims.claim: The checked audit documentation does not explicitly identify events for applying or changing a label on an Engage community.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage sensitivity labels audit log activities community label changed applied; opened audit-log-activities and searched Engage, Yammer and label operations. The Engage table names no label event; general group-label auditing points to Entra without naming an Engage-specific event.

claims.claim: The checked sources publish no Engage-community-specific labeling license beyond the general Purview and group-label requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage community sensitivity labels license licensing Microsoft Entra P1; opened community-sensitivity-labeling, Purview service description, get-started-with-sensitivity-labels and groups-assign-sensitivity-labels. Found general labeling plans and Entra P1, not an Engage-specific SKU.

claims.claim: The roadmap associates this feature with Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Purview"]

claims.claim: The Manual Sensitivity Labeling table also lists OneDrive for Business Plan 2, EMS E3/E5, Office 365 E5/A5/E3/A3 and AIP Plans 1 and 2 as Included.
claims.quote: OneDrive for Business (Plan 2) | Enterprise Mobility + Security E3/E5 | Office 365 E5/A5/E3/A3 | AIP Plan 1, AIP Plan 2 ... | Manual Sensitivity Labeling | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |

claims.claim: The Purview container documentation says to wait at least 24 hours for modified site and group settings to replicate.
claims.quote: If you do, remember to wait at least 24 hours for the changes to replicate to all containers that have the label applied.

claims.claim: The Groups & sites label wizard exposes Privacy and External user access settings.
claims.quote: Privacy and external user access settings to configure the Privacy and External users access settings.
